data.headline: US probes TSMC over possible Huawei ties: Report
data.summary: The United States Commerce Department has launched an investigation into Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), following reports of potential collaboration with Chinese tech giant Huawei. This probe centers on whether TSMC's activities might violate US export controls. TSMC has announced that it is taking "prompt action" to address the concerns. Huawei has been banned from purchasing chips manufactured using US equipment since 2020 as part of broader US national security measures. Catalysts co-hosts Seana Smith and Madison Mills break down the details. To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Catalysts here. data.headline: TSMC stock hits new high after posting forecast-beating earnings
data.summary: Taipei-listed shares in TSMC hit a record high on Friday after the chipmaker posted forecast-beating third-quarter earnings and predicted a rosy outlook on strong artificial intelligence (AI) demand.  The company, however, appeared to face some political uncertainty after U.S. media outlet The Information said the U.S. Department of Commerce is probing whether TSMC has been making AI or smartphone chips for China's Huawei, whose access to non-Chinese chips has been severely curtailed due to U.S. export controls.  As the world's largest contract chipmaker, TSMC, whose customers include Apple and Nvidia, has benefited from a surge towards AI across a spectrum of industries.
